title: Much of the ground-truth continuation can't be derived from the inputs, and grading is a binary 'logically equivalent' check
evidence: The reference PDF (gt_16_ref_0.pdf, 12 pages) is the real next section of the World Bank's International Debt Report 2024. Many of its facts and figures appear nowhere in 16_src_0.pdf or 16_src_1.xlsx. Examples: Box 1.4 case studies ('Zambia ... restructure US$6.3 billion', 'Suriname ... new US$650 million 10-year amortizing bond', 'In September 2024, Ukraine ... restructure US$20 billion'); 'Debt owed to the World Bank (IBRD and IDA) increased 12 percent to ... US$170.8 billion'; PNG 'US$246.7 billion' and short-term 'US$109.3 billion' for IDA-eligible countries; 'debt servicing costs climbed to a record of US$971.1 billion'; 'principal repayments rose 12.9 percent to US$698.9 billion'; 'Mexico and Brazil ... US$13.6 and US$9.7 billion'; 'Variable-rate loans account for 57 percent'; 'Total outstanding SDR allocations ... US$235.8 billion'; export-earnings figures 'US$5.5 trillion', '116.9 percent', '190.2 percent'; the IDA operational cutoff 'US$1,335'. The workbook only holds chart series (Fig1.5–1.9, Box1.4–1.6). The grader guidance asks for a 0/1 score on whether the output is 'logically equivalent to the reference answer' and tells the grader to 'check every value generated by the model and determine whether there is corresponding data in the reference answer'. An agent that writes only what the data supports will be missing most of the reference narrative. An agent that writes a fuller narrative has to invent figures, and those won't match the reference. The guidance's line 'Do not consider extra content in the reference answer that is not within instruction requirements' leaves it unclear whether this content counts as required.
confirmation: gt_16_ref_0.pdf contains figures absent from both inputs: '698.9', '6.3 billion', '170.8', '235.8', '1,335' and '57 percent' are found in neither 16_src_0.pdf nor 16_src_1.xlsx, whose sheets are only chart series Fig1.5-1.9 and Box1.4-1.6. fix: Added a grader-guidance note: the reference narrative's outside facts (examples listed) are not required. Completeness means covering every sheet's series in the report's format. Correctness is checked against the spreadsheet data and against the reference where they overlap. Figures that match the reference are allowed, so the reference itself passes.
